the olfactory bulb nor- adrenergic system is important in mediating the induction of Fos in primary olfactory regions in response to pup sensory cues and behavioral interaction, while the induction of FOS in the medial pre- optic area is independent of olfactory bulb norepinephrine.

The main takeaway from our work is that
pup sensory cues and the maternal environment can differentially regulate Fos expression in distinct brain areas of nullipara mice.
pup sensory cues and noradrenergic activation in the olfactory bulb are necessary for the expression of Fos in the primary olfactory areas.
the medial preoptic nucleus is a key brain area for pup-induced activation of Fos protein and that olfactory input is required for this activation.
